name: Chain-of-Abstraction (CoA)
executive_summary: Train the model to decode a reasoning chain with abstract placeholders first, then call domain tools to fill each one in — decoupling general reasoning strategy from the specific tool results it depends on.
description: Addresses a specific inefficiency in interleaved tool-use methods like ReAct: when text generation and API calls alternate step-by-step, the whole reasoning chain has to wait on each tool call before continuing, and the reasoning strategy gets entangled with tool-call-specific results. CoA trains the model (two-stage fine-tuning) to first produce a complete reasoning chain with abstract placeholders (e.g. 'y1 = Calculator(x1 + x2)') without waiting for real values, then reifies every placeholder with actual tool calls afterward, which can be parallelized. This also makes the learned reasoning strategy more robust to shifts in the underlying domain knowledge, since the abstract chain doesn't hard-code specific facts.
when_to_use: Multi-step tool-use tasks where the reasoning structure is reusable across many different specific fact values (e.g. the same arithmetic strategy applied to different numbers), and you control fine-tuning.
when_not_to_use: Working with a fixed, already-trained model with no fine-tuning access — ReAct's interleaved prompting approach is the inference-time-only alternative.
known_pitfalls: Like Toolformer and APAR, this is a training-time technique, not a drop-in prompting pattern for an off-the-shelf model.

primary_source.authors: Gao, Dwivedi-Yu, Yu, Tan, Pasunuru, Golovneva, Sinha, Celikyilmaz, Bosselut, Wang
primary_source.title: Efficient Tool Use with Chain-of-Abstraction Reasoning
